questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a real-time, allocator with per-thread regions, lock-free structures, and cross-thread reclamation. It probes NUMA topology awareness and worst-case latency guarantees under burst.

## Key Concepts

- Per-thread arenas and size-class pools
- Lock-free freelists with ABA avoidance
- Epoch-based reclamation for cross-thread frees
- NUMA affinity and cache-line alignment
- Fragmentation control and tail latency

## Code Example

```c
typedef struct Allocator Allocator;
void *rt_alloc(Allocator *a, size_t n);
void rt_free(Allocator *a, void *p);
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you validate deterministic latency under microbursts?
- How would you extend to support larger allocations while preserving real-time bounds?

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical memory allocator design under NUMA pressure, focusing on stability, ABA avoidance, and performance with real-time burst workloads.

## Key Concepts
- NUMA locality and per-node memory pools
- Slab/arena allocation strategies
- Hazard pointers for safe memory reclamation
- Cache-line alignment and padding to avoid false sharing
- Cross-socket refill mechanisms and work-stealing

## Code Example
```c
// Skeleton API: slab_alloc, slab_free
typedef struct slab { /* block metadata */ } slab_t;
void* slab_alloc(size_t sz); // 4KB blocks
void slab_free(void* ptr);
```

## Microbenchmark Design
The benchmark would simulate bursty allocations across sockets with threads performing rapid alloc/free cycles, measuring throughput under NUMA-local vs cross-socket memory access patterns.
